To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have designed a dictionary-based fast transform algorithm, StarNT, and a domain-specific text compression utility based on it.

(1) a fast transform algorithm can be used to improve the compression performance of a lossless compressor; (2) a dictionary-based fast transform algorithm can achieve superior compression ratio compared to BWT and PGM based algorithms; (3) a ternary search tree based fast text transform algorithm can be implemented in a way that its encoding time overhead is negligible.

StarNT is a novel dictionary-based fast loss-less text transform algorithm, which achieves a superior compression performance than almost all the recent efforts based on Burrows-Wheeler Transform (BWT) and Prediction by Partial Matching (PPM), and that StarZip is a lossless text compression tool based on StarNT, which utilizes domain-specific dictionaries embedded in the utility to achieve an average improvement in BPC over bzip2, gzip, and PPMD.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following aspects of the text compression problem: (1) the design and implementation of a dictionary-based fast transform; (2) the design and development of a domain-specific compression utility; and (3) the design and analysis of the dictionary construction algorithm.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have designed a new dictionary-based lossless text compression algorithm, which achieves a better compression ratio than the state of the art algorithms.
, with a static dictionary, StarNT and StarZip can achieve superior compression performance and fast compression speed at the same time.
we have developed a fast and high-performance text compression utility for a wide range of applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a dictionary-based fast transform algorithm is able to achieve a better compression ratio than BWT or PPM-based algorithms, and the compression time can be significantly reduced.
dictionary-based text compression can be fast enough to be deployed in a wide range of applications, and the compression ratio can be further improved by using domain-specific static dictionaries.
, for a given domain, a static dictionary-based fast transform can significantly boost the compression performance of the backend compressor, and the time overhead is negligible.
